title: Prime-to-ell alteration category and topology
statement:
Let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme, meaning that it admits a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and let $\ell$ be a prime. Define $\operatorname{alt}/S$ to have as objects the morphisms $T\to S$ of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] with $T$ reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme], such that every generic point of an irreducible component [def-weil-irreducible-components] of $T$ maps to a generic point of an irreducible component of $S$ and the resulting extension of residue fields is finite [def-weil-residue-field]. Its morphisms are the $S$-morphisms. Here a generic point of a component is a point whose closure is that component.

For a morphism $f:T'\to T$ in this category, say that it is maximally $\ell'$-finite if all residue field extensions at generic points of components of $T'$ are finite and, for each generic point $t$ of a component of $T$ belonging to $f(T')$, there is a generic point $t'$ of a component of $T'$ above $t$ for which $[\kappa(t'):\kappa(t)]$ is prime to $\ell$. An etale family $(T_j\to T)_j$ [def-weil-etale-morphism] is $\ell'$-decomposed if for each $t\in T$ there are $j$ and $t_j\in T_j$ above $t$ with $[\kappa(t_j):\kappa(t)]$ finite and prime to $\ell$. It is completely decomposed if these points can be chosen with $\kappa(t)\to\kappa(t_j)$ an isomorphism.

The topology of $\ell'$-alterations on $\operatorname{alt}/S$ is the smallest Grothendieck topology [def-weil-pbc-topos] for which the sieves generated by (i) the $\ell'$-decomposed etale families and (ii) the singleton families consisting of a proper surjective maximally $\ell'$-finite morphism are covering. Proper and surjective mean [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism]. A family is covering if its generated sieve is covering, where its generated sieve consists of the morphisms factoring through some member of the family. A family $(A_i\to T)_i$ refines $(B_j\to T)_j$ if for each $i$ there are $j(i)$ and a $T$-morphism $A_i\to B_{j(i)}$.
